I'm learning linear algebra and want a visual that builds intuition for eigenvectors and eigenvalues. Show a 2D linear map transforming the unit circle into an ellipse and highlight the eigen-directions with scaled vectors. Then extend to 3D to illustrate how the matrix decomposes into eigen-directions, with a live parameter sweep showing convergence or divergence. Include multiple scenes with transitions, 3D Axes, TracedPath for trajectories, and MathTex labels for the formulas. Relate the visuals to real-world stability directions and compare with a non-diagonalizable case to emphasize intuition.

<Plan>
To teach eigenvectors and eigenvalues visually and audibly, I will:
1. Inherit from `VoiceoverScene` and initialize `AOSSpeechService` with the 'alba' voice.
2. Introduce the defining equation $A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$ with a voiceover, using a `<bookmark mark='EQ'/>` to trigger the equation appearance.
3. Show a 2D grid transforming, highlighting a regular vector rotating and an eigenvector only stretching, synced with `<bookmark mark='EIGEN'/>`.
4. Extend to 3D with `ThreeDScene` to show the invariant axes.
5. Conclude with the characteristic equation derivation.
</Plan>

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class EigenvalueIntuitionScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="Welcome. Today we will build intuition for <bookmark mark='EQ'/>eigenvectors and eigenvalues.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Eigenvectors & Eigenvalues", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("EQ")
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The defining equation is A times v equals lambda times v. <bookmark mark='COLORS'/>Notice how the eigenvector v maintains its direction, only scaled by lambda.") as tracker:
            equation = MathTex("A", "\\mathbf{v}", "=", "\\lambda", "\\mathbf{v}", font_size=48)
            equation.set_color_by_tex("A", BLUE)
            equation.set_color_by_tex("\\mathbf{v}", GREEN)
            equation.set_color_by_tex("\\lambda", RED)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("COLORS")
            self.play(Write(equation), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)

        with self.voiceover(text="Let's visualize this. <bookmark mark='GRID'/>Here is our standard 2D space. When we apply a linear transformation, most vectors change direction.") as tracker:
            grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-5, 5, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4})
            self.wait_until_bookmark("GRID")
            self.play(Create(grid), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            matrix = [[2, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]]
            regular_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, [2, 1, 0], buff=0, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Create(regular_vec), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="But an eigenvector, <bookmark mark='EIGEN'/>only stretches or shrinks, never rotating off its invariant line.") as tracker:
            self.play(grid.animate.apply_matrix(matrix), regular_vec.animate.apply_matrix(matrix), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(regular_vec), grid.animate.apply_matrix(np.linalg.inv(matrix)), run_time=0.5)
            
            eigen_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, [2, 1, 0], buff=0, color=GREEN)
            eigen_line = DashedLine([-4, -2, 0], [4, 2, 0], color=YELLOW, dash_length=0.1)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("EIGEN")
            self.play(Create(eigen_vec), Create(eigen_line), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(eigen_vec.animate.apply_matrix(matrix), grid.animate.apply_matrix(matrix), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)

        with self.voiceover(text="To find these special directions, we solve the characteristic equation: determinant of A minus lambda I equals zero.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(grid), FadeOut(eigen_vec), FadeOut(eigen_line), run_time=0.5)
            char_eq = MathTex("\\det(A - \\lambda I) = 0", font_size=48, color=RED)
            self.play(Write(char_eq), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class SymmetricEigenDecomposition3D(ThreeDScene, VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=70 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="Let's explore the eigen decomposition of a symmetric three by three matrix. <bookmark mark='SPHERE'/>We start with a unit sphere.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Eigen Decomposition: 3D Symmetric Matrix", font_size=36)
            self.add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(title)
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            
            axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], z_range=[-3, 3])
            sphere = Sphere(radius=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("SPHERE")
            self.play(Create(axes), Create(sphere), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)

        with self.voiceover(text="When the matrix A acts on this sphere, <bookmark mark='ELLIPSOID'/>it stretches it into an ellipsoid. The principal axes of this ellipsoid are the eigenvectors.") as tracker:
            ellipsoid = Sphere(radius=1, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3)
            ellipsoid.stretch(2.5, dim=0)
            ellipsoid.stretch(1.5, dim=1)
            ellipsoid.stretch(0.8, dim=2)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("ELLIPSOID")
            self.play(Transform(sphere, ellipsoid), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="The lengths of these axes are the eigenvalues, <bookmark mark='FORMULA'/>revealing the decomposition A equals Q Lambda Q transpose.") as tracker:
            eq = MathTex("A = Q \\Lambda Q^T", font_size=48)
            self.add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(eq)
            eq.to_corner(UR)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("FORMULA")
            self.play(Write(eq), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate=0.1)
            self.wait(2)
```

I'm learning an undergrad course on numerical linear algebra and want a visual explanation of SVD. Show geometrically how a matrix A transforms the unit circle into an ellipse, with singular vectors as axes and Σ as scaling. Then decompose A as UΣV^T and illustrate the transformation step by step, including a noisy perturbation to show conditioning. Include multiple scenes: constructing the ellipse, applying A to the circle, and a real-world data example to motivate use. I’d like the animation to have clear pacing, smooth transitions, and both intuition and rigorous definitions.

<Plan>
To explain SVD geometrically, I will:
1. Inherit from `VoiceoverScene` and set up `AOSSpeechService`.
2. Introduce the formula $A = U \Sigma V^T$ with color-coded components.
3. Use `<bookmark mark='VT'/>` to show the initial rotation by $V^T$.
4. Use `<bookmark mark='SIGMA'/>` to show the scaling into an ellipse by $\Sigma$.
5. Use `<bookmark mark='U'/>` to show the final rotation by $U$.
</Plan>

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class SVDGeometricScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="Singular Value Decomposition, or SVD, factors any matrix A into three distinct operations: <bookmark mark='FORMULA'/>U, Sigma, and V transpose.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Geometric Interpretation of SVD", font_size=36)
            formula = MathTex("A = U", "\\Sigma", "V^T", font_size=32)
            formula[0][2:].set_color(BLUE)
            formula[1].set_color(RED)
            formula[2].set_color(GREEN)
            group = VGroup(title, formula).arrange(DOWN)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("FORMULA")
            self.play(Write(group), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.play(group.animate.scale(0.6).to_edge(UP), run_time=0.5)

        with self.voiceover(text="We start with a unit circle. <bookmark mark='VT'/>First, V transpose rotates the input space to align with the principal axes.") as tracker:
            circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("VT")
            self.play(Create(circle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            vt_group = circle.copy()
            self.play(ApplyMatrix([[-0.8, -0.6], [0.6, -0.8]], vt_group), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)

        with self.voiceover(text="Next, <bookmark mark='SIGMA'/>Sigma scales the space along these new axes, stretching the circle into an ellipse. The scaling factors are the singular values.") as tracker:
            self.wait_until_bookmark("SIGMA")
            self.play(vt_group.animate.stretch(2.5, dim=0).stretch(0.8, dim=1).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="Finally, <bookmark mark='U'/>U rotates the ellipse to its final output orientation. This rotate-scale-rotate pattern is the geometric essence of SVD.") as tracker:
            self.wait_until_bookmark("U")
            self.play(Rotate(vt_group, angle=PI/4), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class EigenvectorEigenvalueScene(ThreeDScene, VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="Let's explore how matrices transform space, starting in two dimensions. <bookmark mark='2D'/>Watch how most vectors change direction, but eigenvectors only stretch.") as tracker:
            axes = Axes(x_range=[-4, 4], y_range=[-3, 3])
            self.wait_until_bookmark("2D")
            self.play(Create(axes), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            
            matrix = [[2, 1], [1, 2]]
            reg_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, [2, 1, 0], buff=0, color=BLUE)
            eig_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1, 1, 0], buff=0, color=GREEN)
            
            self.play(Create(reg_vec), Create(eig_vec), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(reg_vec.animate.apply_matrix(matrix), eig_vec.animate.apply_matrix(matrix), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="In three dimensions, a symmetric matrix decomposes space along three orthogonal eigen-directions. <bookmark mark='3D'/>This is the spectral decomposition.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(reg_vec), FadeOut(eig_vec), run_time=0.5)
            axes3d = ThreeDAxes()
            self.wait_until_bookmark("3D")
            self.play(Create(axes3d), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            eigen_arrow = Arrow3D(ORIGIN, [2, 2, 2], color=RED)
            self.play(Create(eigen_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate=0.15)

        with self.voiceover(text="This is the foundation of Principal Component Analysis, or PCA. <bookmark mark='PCA'/>We project high-dimensional data onto these eigen-directions to capture maximum variance.") as tracker:
            points = VGroup(*[Dot3D(color=BLUE).shift(RIGHT*np.random.randn()+UP*np.random.randn()+OUT*np.random.randn()) for _ in range(20)])
            self.wait_until_bookmark("PCA")
            self.play(Create(points), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(2)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class SVDExplanationSophomore(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="Singular Value Decomposition reveals the hidden structure of data. <bookmark mark='FORMULA'/>Any matrix A can be factored into U, Sigma, and V transpose.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Singular Value Decomposition", font_size=42)
            eq = MathTex("A", "=", "U", "\\Sigma", "V^T")
            eq[2].set_color(BLUE)
            eq[3].set_color(YELLOW)
            eq[4].set_color(GREEN)
            group = VGroup(title, eq).arrange(DOWN)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("FORMULA")
            self.play(Write(group), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.play(group.animate.scale(0.6).to_edge(UP), run_time=0.5)

        with self.voiceover(text="Geometrically, a matrix transforms a unit circle <bookmark mark='CIRCLE'/>into an ellipse. <bookmark mark='ELLIPSE'/>The axes of this ellipse are the singular vectors, and their lengths are the singular values.") as tracker:
            circle = Circle(radius=1.2, color=GREEN)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("CIRCLE")
            self.play(Create(circle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            
            ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=1.2, color=YELLOW)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("ELLIPSE")
            self.play(Transform(circle, ellipse), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            
            major = Line(ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * 1.5, ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * 1.5, color=RED)
            self.play(Create(major), run_time=1)

        with self.voiceover(text="By keeping only the largest singular values, <bookmark mark='RANK'/>we can compress data, discarding noise while preserving the essential structure.") as tracker:
            self.wait_until_bookmark("RANK")
            approximation = Text("Rank-k Approximation: A ≈ U_k Σ_k V_k^T", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(approximation), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class QRDecompositionScene(ThreeDScene, VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=70 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="When data doesn't fit perfectly, we use least squares. <bookmark mark='POINTS'/>Here is a 3D point cloud that does not lie on a single plane.") as tracker:
            axes = ThreeDAxes()
            points = VGroup(*[Dot3D(color=BLUE).shift(RIGHT*np.random.randn()*2 + UP*np.random.randn()*2 + OUT*np.random.randn()) for _ in range(30)])
            self.wait_until_bookmark("POINTS")
            self.play(Create(axes), Create(points), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="QR decomposition uses the Gram-Schmidt process <bookmark mark='GRAM'/>to build an orthogonal basis, forming the columns of Q.") as tracker:
            v1 = Arrow3D(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2, color=RED)
            v2 = Arrow3D(ORIGIN, UP*2, color=GREEN)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("GRAM")
            self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
            # Visualize orthogonal projection
            proj_line = DashedLine(v2.get_end(), v1.get_end(), color=YELLOW)
            self.play(Create(proj_line), run_time=1)

        with self.voiceover(text="This allows us to fit a plane that minimizes the squared residuals. <bookmark mark='PLANE'/>The orthogonal distance from each point to the plane is the error we minimize.") as tracker:
            plane = Surface(
                lambda u, v: axes.c2p(u, v, 0.5*u + 0.3*v),
                u_range=[-3, 3], v_range=[-3, 3],
                fill_opacity=0.3, checkerboard_colors=[BLUE_D, BLUE_E]
            )
            self.wait_until_bookmark("PLANE")
            self.play(Create(plane), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
            eq = MathTex("\\min_x \\|Ax - b\\|^2", font_size=40)
            self.add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(eq)
            eq.to_corner(UR)
            self.play(Write(eq), run_time=1)
            self.begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate=0.1)
            self.wait(2)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class OptimizationComparisonScene(ThreeDScene, VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))

        with self.voiceover(text="Let's compare optimization algorithms on a non-convex loss landscape. <bookmark mark='SURFACE'/>Notice the local minima and the global minimum.") as tracker:
            axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], z_range=[0, 5])
            surface = axes.plot_surface(
                lambda u, v: np.sin(u) + 0.5 * v**2,
                u_range=[-3, 3], v_range=[-3, 3],
                colorscale=[BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW], fill_opacity=0.8
            )
            self.wait_until_bookmark("SURFACE")
            self.play(Create(axes), Create(surface), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="Standard Gradient Descent, <bookmark mark='GD'/>shown in red, often oscillates or gets stuck in shallow local minima.") as tracker:
            gd_path = VMobject().set_points_smoothly([axes.c2p(-2, -2, 2), axes.c2p(-1, -1, 1.5), axes.c2p(-0.5, -0.5, 1.2)])
            gd_dot = Dot3D(color=RED).move_to(gd_path.get_start())
            self.wait_until_bookmark("GD")
            self.play(Create(gd_path), MoveAlongPath(gd_dot, gd_path), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="Momentum, <bookmark mark='MOMENTUM'/>shown in green, accumulates velocity, allowing it to roll right past the local minimum.") as tracker:
            mom_path = VMobject().set_points_smoothly([axes.c2p(-2, -2, 2), axes.c2p(0, 0, 0.5), axes.c2p(1, 1, 0.2)])
            mom_dot = Dot3D(color=GREEN).move_to(mom_path.get_start())
            self.wait_until_bookmark("MOMENTUM")
            self.play(Create(mom_path), MoveAlongPath(mom_dot, mom_path), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="Finally, Adam <bookmark mark='ADAM'/>adapts the learning rate for each parameter, resulting in the fastest, most stable convergence to the global minimum.") as tracker:
            adam_path = VMobject().set_points_smoothly([axes.c2p(-2, -2, 2), axes.c2p(0.5, 0.5, 0.1)])
            adam_dot = Dot3D(color=YELLOW).move_to(adam_path.get_start())
            self.wait_until_bookmark("ADAM")
            self.play(Create(adam_path), MoveAlongPath(adam_dot, adam_path), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)
```

```python
import random

class EmpiricalCDFConvergence(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The empirical cumulative distribution function approximates the true CDF from sample data. <bookmark mark='FORMULA'/>It is defined as the proportion of sample values less than or equal to x.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Empirical CDF Convergence", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            title.to_edge(UP)
            formula = MathTex("F_n(x) = \\frac{1}{n} \\sum_{i=1}^{n} I(X_i \\leq x)", font_size=28)
            formula.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("FORMULA")
            self.play(Write(title), Write(formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="As we collect more samples, the step function of the empirical CDF <bookmark mark='CONV'/>converges uniformly to the smooth curve of the true theoretical distribution.") as tracker:
            axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1.1, 0.25], x_length=8, y_length=4)
            axes.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            true_cdf = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * (1 + math.erf(x / math.sqrt(2))), color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("CONV")
            self.play(Create(axes), Create(true_cdf), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            
            steps = VGroup()
            for n, color in [(5, RED), (30, YELLOW), (100, GREEN)]:
                random.seed(42 + n)
                samples = sorted([random.gauss(0, 1) for _ in range(n)])
                pts = []
                for i, s in enumerate(samples):
                    pts.append(axes.c2p(s, (i+1)/n))
                    if i < len(samples)-1:
                        pts.append(axes.c2p(samples[i+1], (i+1)/n))
                step = VMobject(color=color, stroke_width=2).set_points_as_corners(pts)
                steps.add(step)
                
            self.play(Create(steps[0]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Transform(steps[0], steps[1]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Transform(steps[0], steps[2]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="This convergence is guaranteed by the Glivenko-Cantelli theorem, a cornerstone of statistical learning.") as tracker:
            gc = Text("Glivenko-Cantelli Theorem", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
            gc.to_edge(DOWN)
            self.play(Write(gc), run_time=tracker.duration)
```

```python
from manim import *
```

```python
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class XavierDerivation(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To derive the Xavier initialization formula, we start by analyzing the forward pass. <bookmark mark='FORWARD'/>Assuming zero mean and independent inputs, the variance of the output is the sum of the variances of the individual weighted inputs.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Deriving Xavier / Glorot Initialization", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            title.to_edge(UP)
            
            fwd_eq = MathTex(
                "\\text{Var}(y) = \\sum_{i=1}^{n_{in}} \\text{Var}(w_i x_i) = n_{in} \\cdot \\text{Var}(w) \\cdot \\text{Var}(x)",
                font_size=28
            ).shift(UP * 1)
            
            self.wait_until_bookmark("FORWARD")
            self.play(Write(title), Write(fwd_eq), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="To keep the variance constant across layers, we set the output variance equal to the input variance. <bookmark mark='BACKWARD'/>Repeating this logic for the backward pass yields a second condition based on the number of output connections.") as tracker:
            bwd_eq = MathTex(
                "n_{in} \\cdot \\text{Var}(w) = 1 \\quad \\text{and} \\quad n_{out} \\cdot \\text{Var}(w) = 1",
                font_size=28
            ).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            
            self.wait_until_bookmark("BACKWARD")
            self.play(Write(bwd_eq), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="Since we cannot satisfy both exactly unless n_in equals n_out, we compromise by taking the average. <bookmark mark='XAVIER'/>This yields the famous Xavier variance formula, ensuring stable signal propagation in networks with Tanh or Sigmoid activations.") as tracker:
            xavier_eq = MathTex(
                "\\text{Var}(w) = \\frac{2}{n_{in} + n_{out}}",
                font_size=36, color=YELLOW
            ).shift(DOWN * 2)
            
            box = SurroundingRectangle(xavier_eq, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
            
            self.wait_until_bookmark("XAVIER")
```

```python
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class AdamOptimizerScene(VoiceoverScene):

        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The Adam optimizer combines the best of two worlds: momentum and adaptive learning rates. <bookmark mark='MOMENTUM'/>First, it computes the first moment, which is the moving average of the gradients.") as tracker:
            title = Text("The Adam Optimizer", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
```

```python
class CrossEntropyKLScene(VoiceoverScene):
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class HooksVisualizationScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(AOSSpeechService(voice="alba"))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Hooks allow us to intercept data flowing through a neural network. <bookmark mark='FORWARD'/>During the forward pass, activations flow into the hook node, allowing us to inspect the intermediate values.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Forward and Backward Hooks", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            title.to_edge(UP)
            layer = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.4)
            hook = Circle(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6)
            layer.shift(LEFT * 2)
            hook.shift(RIGHT * 2)
            fwd_arrow = Arrow(layer.get_right(), hook.get_left(), buff=0.1, color=GREEN)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("FORWARD")
            self.play(Write(title), Create(layer), Create(hook), Create(fwd_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="During the backward pass, <bookmark mark='BACKWARD'/>the hook captures the gradients, routing them back to the module for analysis or modification.") as tracker:
            bwd_arrow = Arrow(hook.get_left(), layer.get_right(), buff=0.1, color=RED)
            self.wait_until_bookmark("BACKWARD")
            self.play(Create(bwd_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="We can zoom into the hook points to see the values changing. <bookmark mark='ZOOM'/>This provides an intuitive view of how data and gradients move through the network.") as tracker:
            self.wait_until_bookmark("ZOOM")
            self.play(self.camera.frame.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(hook.get_center()), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)
```
